key_insight: A self-supervised graph transformer infers spatial, single-cell-level interactions directly from imaging-based spatial transcriptomics, overcoming limited gene panels and eliminating the need for known ligand–receptor pairs.
problem_solved: Imaging-based spatial transcriptomics typically measures a limited gene panel, making ligand–receptor-based interaction inference unreliable; this method recovers cell–cell interaction signals from sparse, spatially resolved data without curated interaction priors.
method: Build spatial cell graphs that combine cell coordinates and measured expression, representing local neighborhoods as graph structure.
Train a graph transformer with self-supervised objectives (e.g., masked feature reconstruction / contrastive learning) to learn context-aware cell embeddings without labels.
Use learned embeddings to score or predict interaction edges at single-cell resolution, robust to missing genes and independent of predefined ligand–receptor lists.
impact: Enables AI/ML practitioners to apply graph-based, self-supervised models to spatial omics tasks—unlocking discovery of cell–cell interactions from sparse measurements and reducing dependence on curated biological priors.
